name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years of continuous, immediate migratory residence in Peru (raised from 2 years under the prior Ley N.26574).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of continuous legal residence in Peru.

requirements.blocker_text: Lawful annual income of at least 10 UIT (S/55,000 in 2026), with formal tax-compliance evidence.
Examination covering Spanish (or, per the new law, optionally an indigenous language) proficiency, Peruvian history, geography, the Constitution, culture, and current affairs.
Interpol background check and a valid passport from the country of origin.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous migratory residence
Proof of annual income of 10 UIT with tax-compliance records
Naturalisation exam pass (language, history, geography, Constitution, culture, current affairs)
Valid passport from country of origin

sources.title: El Peruano (Peru's official state gazette) -- 'Ley de Nacionalidad: nuevos requisitos para obtener, recuperar o renunciar a la ciudadania peruana': Ley N.32421 raises naturalisation residence from 2 to 5 years, requires 10 UIT annual income with tax compliance, adds a language/history/geography/Constitution/culture/current-affairs exam, Interpol check, valid passport, processing up to 18 months (extendable by 6)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Peru). STATUS: DRAFT, LIVE LEGAL TRANSITION -- Ley N.32421 ('Nueva Ley de Nacionalidad') was promulgated in August 2025, reported directly by Peru's own official gazette (El Peruano, tier-1) as raising naturalisation residence from 2 to 5 years and adding the 10 UIT/exam requirements described here. However, a separate tier-3 consultancy source (tramitesperu.com, dated 2026) describes naturalisation as STILL operating under the OLD Ley N.26574 (2-year residence) with Ley 32421 'pendiente de reglamentacion' (pending its implementing regulation) as of that source's writing -- a direct conflict between an official-gazette report that the law's terms apply and a practitioner report that the old rules remain operative pending regulation. Modeled here using the new Ley 32421 terms since El Peruano is the tier-1 source and over a year has passed since promulgation, but held to DRAFT specifically because of this unresolved transition, not because the underlying source is weak. A 'recuperacion' (recovery) track for former citizens who lost Peruvian nationality is mentioned in the same Ley 32421 reporting but no requirement detail was found -- disclosed as a gap, not modeled as a separate route in this pass.
